description: Asking which keychains exist / where passwords are stored maps to security/list_keychains (security list-keychains), a read-only listing of keychain file paths. Not a credential lookup and not a settings read. No confirmation.
prompt: What keychains do I have on this Mac?

description: Asking whether a saved password EXISTS for an app/service (without asking to reveal it) maps to security/find_credential — the metadata-only generic-password lookup — not find_internet_credential (which is for website/server logins). Read-only and secret-safe; no confirmation.
prompt: Do I have a saved password stored for the service called AirPort? I just want to know if it exists and what account it's under, not the password itself.

description: Asking whether a saved login exists for a website/server maps to security/find_internet_credential (metadata-only internet-password lookup), distinct from find_credential (generic app/service passwords). Read-only, secret-safe.
prompt: Have I saved a login for the website example.com in my keychain?

description: MANUAL (reads the real login keychain; may trigger a keychain access prompt). Looks up an existing saved password's metadata and confirms the response is framed as secret-safe. The human MUST eyeball the output to verify the actual password value does NOT appear — only service/account/label/dates should. Substitute a service you actually have saved (e.g. a Wi-Fi network name).
prompt: Look up the saved password metadata for the service 'AirPort' — tell me the account and when it was saved, but do not show the password.
